newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK BROKER REPS TAKE BREAK IN ECON MEETING.
newsitem.headline: GREEK BROKER REPS TAKE BREAK IN ECON MEETING.

text.p: Representatives of the Greek stockbrokers association took a break in their late night talks with national economy ministry officials aimed at resolving a row over settlements with the bourse's clearing house.
The row erupted after Delta Securities was charged with fraud last week. The brokers have refused to trade for two days, virtually closing the Athens stock exchange.

"We made some suggestions. It is a developing process. We hope a solution will be found," the president of the Association of Athens Stock Exchange Members (SMEHA), Panagiotis Kondalexis told reporters.
It was unclear which side had requested the break but the SMEHA representatives said talks with deputy national economy minister Apostolos Fotiades would resume shortly.

SMEHA's 65 members agreed earlier to propose to the national economy ministry that trades between 11 brokers and Delta over the past 10 days be nullified. This would largely balance the 2.6 billion drachma default by Delta in settlements last week.
It was still unclear whether the bourse would operate on Tuesday.
